The WIPPES Act (H.R. 2269) exemplifies bureaucratic overreach disguised as environmental protection. Mandating "Do Not Flush" labels on wipes adds regulatory bloat while ignoring the core issue: consumers already know not to flush non-flushables.

Section 2(b) forces manufacturers into costly packaging redesigns for cylindrical containers, flip lids, and bulk packaging—a $55M annual burden passed to taxpayers through higher prices. Meanwhile, wastewater systems remain underfunded because D.C. prioritizes performative labeling over upgrading infrastructure.

This bill doesn’t fix broken pipes—it just slaps a sticker on the problem while expanding FTC oversight (Section 2(e)). Real solutions require cutting red tape, not adding more.
